result.topic_en: Riemann writes the equations of motion for the small displacements of the aether in light phenomena (wave equations with a divergence-free condition) and derives a variational formulation in terms of a quadratic potential function X expanded in time, with a surface boundary condition and a Lagrange-multiplier term for the divergence.
result.transcription:
$u_1, u_2, u_3$ die unendlich kleinen Verschiebungen des Aethers parallel den drei Coordinatenaxen
$x_1, x_2, x_3$. — Dann sind die Bewegungsgleichungen für die Lichterscheinungen
$\frac{\partial^2 u_1}{\partial t^2} - \alpha\alpha\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_1}{\partial x_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u_1}{\partial x_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u_1}{\partial x_3^2}\right)=0$ ; $\frac{\partial^2 u_2}{\partial t^2} - \alpha\alpha\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_2}{\partial x_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u_2}{\partial x_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u_2}{\partial x_3^2}\right)=0$ ; $\frac{\partial^2 u_3}{\partial t^2} - \alpha\alpha\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_3}{\partial x_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u_3}{\partial x_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u_3}{\partial x_3^2}\right)=0$
∂ [?]
$\frac{\partial u_1}{\partial x_1}+\frac{\partial u_2}{\partial x_2}+\frac{\partial u_3}{\partial x_3}=0$
[-also
$\int\left\{\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_1}{\partial t^2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_2}{\partial t^2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_3}{\partial t^2}\right)^2-\alpha\alpha\sum_{h,k}\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial x_k^2}\cdot\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial t^2}\right\}dx_1dx_2dx_3=0$
$=-\alpha\alpha\int\sum_{h,k}\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial t^2}\frac{\partial u_h}{\partial x_k}dx_{k+1}dx_{k+2}+\int\left\{\sum_h\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial t^2}\right)^2+\alpha\alpha\sum_{h,k}\frac{\partial u_h}{\partial x_k}\cdot\frac{\partial^3 u_h}{\partial x_k\partial t^2}\right\}dx_1dx_2dx_3=0$
Setzt man $\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^2 X}{\partial t^2}dt^2=\frac{1}{2}\int\alpha\alpha\sum_{h,k}\left\{\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial x_k\partial t}\right)^2+\frac{\partial u_h}{\partial x_k}\cdot\frac{\partial^3 u_h}{\partial x_k\partial t^2}\right\}dt^2dx_1dx_2dx_3$
also $X=\frac{1}{2}\int\alpha\alpha\sum\left(\frac{\partial u_h}{\partial x_k}\right)^2dx_1dx_2dx_3$
$X_{t+dt}=X+\frac{\partial X}{\partial t}dt+\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^2 X}{\partial t^2}dt^2+\frac{1}{2\cdot3}\frac{\partial^3 X}{\partial t^3}dt^3+\dots$-]
Multiplicirt man diese drei Gleichungen resp. mit $\delta\frac{\partial^2 u_1}{\partial t^2}$, $\delta\frac{\partial^2 u_2}{\partial t^2}$ u. $\delta\frac{\partial^2 u_3}{\partial t^2}$
[-$\int\sum_{h,k}\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial t^2}\cdot\delta\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial t^2}$-]
{+$+\beta\beta\int$+}
$H=\int\left\{\sum\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial t^2}\cdot\delta\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial t^2}-\alpha\alpha\sum_{h,k}\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial x_k^2}\cdot\delta\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial t^2}\right\}dx_1dx_2dx_3=0$
$=-\alpha\alpha\int\sum_{h,k}\frac{\partial u_h}{\partial x_k}\delta\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}dx_{k+1}dx_{k+2}+\int\left\{\frac{1}{2}\sum\delta\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial t^2}\right)^2+\alpha\alpha\sum\frac{\partial u_h}{\partial x_k}\delta\frac{\partial^3 u_h}{\partial x_k\partial t^2}\right\}dx_1dx_2dx_3=0$
Setzt man
$\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^2 X}{\partial t^2}=\int\alpha\alpha\sum\left\{\left(\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x_k\partial t}\right)^2+\frac{\partial u_h}{\partial x_k}\cdot\frac{\partial^3 u_h}{\partial x_k\partial t^2}\right\}dx_1dx_2dx_3$
also $X=\int\alpha\alpha\sum\left(\frac{\partial u_h}{\partial x_k}\right)^2dx_1dx_2dx_3$
Sei $X_{(t+dt)}=X+\frac{\partial X}{\partial t}dt+\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^2 X}{\partial t^2}dt^2+\frac{1}{2\cdot3}\frac{\partial^3 X}{\partial t^3}dt^3+\dots$
So ist $\frac{\delta X_{(t+dt)}}{\delta\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}}=\frac{1}{2}dt^2\frac{\delta\frac{\partial^2 X}{\partial t^2}}{\delta\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}}=dt^2\int\alpha\alpha\sum\frac{\partial u_h}{\partial x_k}\frac{\delta\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial x_k\partial t^2}}{\delta\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}}dx_1dx_2dx_3$
Demnach
$H=-\alpha\alpha\int\sum\frac{\partial u_h}{\partial x_k}\delta\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}dx_{k+1}dx_{k+2}+\frac{\delta}{\delta\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}dt^2}\left\{\int\frac{1}{2}\sum\left(d_t\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\right)^2dx_1dx_2dx_3+X_{(t+dt)}\right\}=0$
Es soll nun eine Bedingung statt finden, {+derzufolge+} [-die-] die Werthe an den Oberflächen der
Körper verschwinden, es geht also die letzte Gleichung in folgende über
$\frac{\delta}{\delta\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}}\left\{\int\frac{1}{2}\sum\left(d_t\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\right)^2dx_1dx_2dx_3+X_{(t+dt)}\right\}$ {+$+\beta\beta\int\left(\frac{\partial u_1}{\partial x_1}+\frac{\partial u_2}{\partial x_2}+\frac{\partial u_3}{\partial x_3}\right)^2dx_1dx_2dx_3$+} $=0$
wo $X_t=\int\alpha\alpha\sum\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial x_k^2}\right)^2dx_1dx_2dx_3$
